subtitle: The Last Flame
confirm_overwrite: Starting over erases this memory. Continue?
confirm_quit: Quit to the main menu? Your progress has been saved.
sword_desc:
A long, slender sword found in your own grave. No name is engraved on it — whoever forged it wanted it forgotten.

Hrolf can temper it with Ash Steel.
stat_spell: Damage: {n} · Cost: a third of your Lume
flask_desc:
Candles lit at an Ember Altar. Burning one restores part of your life, but demands a moment of stillness.

They are relit when you rest. Candle Fragments add more.
msg_no_slots: No free slots. Remove another relic first.
map_legend: Drag or arrows to pan · Q/E or wheel to zoom · Orange dots: Altars · Dashed outlines: unexplored
j_empty: Nothing has been written here yet.
set_remap_note: Choose an action and press the new key (Esc cancels). Arrow keys also move and navigate menus.
set_pad_layout: Gamepad: A jump · X attack · Y heavy · B dodge · RB/LT parry and guard · LB heal · RT spell · ↑ interact · Start pause · Back inventory · RS map
set_data_note: Your save lives in this browser's storage. Clearing site data erases it — export a copy to keep it elsewhere.
msg_import_fail: That text is not a valid save.
rest_text: The flame warms your bones. Your candles are relit and your life returns — but the dead of this region rise again as well.
death_sub_ash: Your ash was left behind, kept by your echo. Touch it again to reclaim it — fall before that, and it is lost.
smith_text:
Blade +{lvl} → +{next}
Cost: {steel} Ash Steel (you have {have}) and {ash} ash (you have {hash}).
smith_max: The blade can take no more tempering. It is as sharp as steel can be.
smith_cap: "Beyond this, only Master Hilde knew how to temper. I don't."
msg_upgraded: The Blade of the Awakened reached +{n}.
msg_altar_lit: Ember Altar kindled — you can travel here.
msg_palace_open: The embers recognise the gate. The Palace opens.
msg_need_embers: Six empty sockets. The gate demands {n} embers (you have {have}).
msg_no_storage: This browser does not allow saving: your game will be lost when you close it.
hint_move: Move: A/D or arrows · Jump: Space · Attack: J · Dodge: L / Shift
hint_attack: Attack: J (with ↑ or ↓ for directional strikes) · Heavy strike: K
hint_heal: Heal: F (uses a candle) · Parry: I at the moment of impact; hold to guard
hint_cracked: The cracked stone holds. You need a stronger blow.
hint_charge: Hold the heavy strike to charge it and shatter the stone.
hint_cracked_wall: There is a cracked wall here. Perhaps one day you will be strong enough to break it.
hint_palace: The Palace gate bears six flame-shaped sockets.
hint_too_high: Too high for a single jump.
hint_gap: The chasm is too wide to jump. Perhaps with another movement…
hint_rest: The Ember Altar: resting restores life and candles and marks your return.
tut_dash: Ash Step: press Dodge in mid-air to launch forward.
tut_spell: Spark: press Q to cast fire (costs Lume, which fills as you strike and parry).
tut_wall: Sentinel's Claw: cling to walls and leap off them.
tut_forge: Forge Strike: hold the heavy strike to charge it — it shatters cracked stone.
tut_double: Moth Wings: jump again in mid-air.
tut_veil: Veil Unwoven: you pass through spectral veils.
tip_guardbreak: The shield charge breaks your guard — dodge!
tip_caedmon_shield: Caedmon's shield is absolute. Parry the white-gleaming strikes to break his posture.
tip_caedmon_broken: His posture is broken! Strike now — a riposte cuts deeper.
tip_automato_back: The furnace on its back is fragile. After the vents roar, the grate glows white — strike it there to make it stagger.
tip_seraphine: Her light does not yield to your blade. Return the light with parries.
victory_more: Continue this memory to return to the final choice and learn another fate.
victory_all: You have seen every fate of Vesperal. Thank you for playing.

The Last Flame

A game by

With thanks

To whoever wakes.
hint_parry_bolts: Crossbow bolts gleam before they fly. A parry at the right instant sends them back.
hint_wall: The chimney walls stand close together. Someone with claws could climb them.
hint_veil: A spectral veil seals the passage. It hums like a lute string.
intro_1: The Lume chose a vessel in every generation. In the last, it chose Queen Seraphine — and the flame began to burn her from within.
intro_2: On a moonless night, they tried to tear it from her. The Lume shattered into six embers, which fled to those the queen loved. Vesperal was buried in ash, and the dead awoke.
ione_meet1: New footsteps in the Sanctuary. They don't drag, like the others. You are awake — truly awake.
ione_meet2: My name is Ione. This is the Last Flame… or what is left of it. My mother burned so that it would burn, and while it burned, the dead slept.
ione_meet3: On the moonless night the Lume fled from her in six embers. They went to the people she loved, and now those people cannot rest. Nor will they let anyone else.
ione_meet4: I cannot see. But I feel the warmth you carry in your chest — it is small, but it is the Lume's. It trusted you. I will trust you too.
ione_meet5: Bring me the six embers. Rest at the Altar whenever you need; its flame still knows you. They say the old gravedigger keeps something beneath the Cemetery. Start there.
ione_ember1: This ember… is steady. It smells of wet steel. Caedmon. He swore to guard it until his last breath — and he kept his word, even past it.
ione_ember2: Hilde. I know her by the heat — her hands were always warm. She taught my mother to hold a hammer. She said it was the only useful advice she had.
ione_ember3: Nurse. Elowen sang me to sleep. This ember still hums, do you hear it? Poor nurse… she never knew how to let anyone grow up.
ione_ember4: Corvin. This one thrums like a string. He played my mother a song that was not allowed to be played. He never told me its name.
ione_ember5: The bishop. It is cold inside. He taught my mother to read, you know. Sometimes the ones who teach us to read are the ones who lie to us most.
ione_ember6: My father. It weighs so much… I knew it would be the last. He never knew how to let go of anything.
ione_spell1: Wait. The Last Flame answered the ember. There is a spark too many here — it wants to go with you.
ione_spell2: Close your hand around it and release it forward. It spends itself, but it grows back every time you strike or parry a blow.
ione_ribbon: Take this as well. It is the ribbon I wore in my hair. They say ash clings to what is mine — perhaps it will bring you more.
ione_letters_ask: You carry papers. I feel the wax — red. It is my mother's. Will you read them to me?
ione_letters1: (You read the three letters slowly. Ione does not interrupt you.)
ione_letters2: …So that was why. At the end, she did not think of me. I believed she had forgotten. She remembered too much.
ione_letters3: Morning. A light that is born and dies every day, and that no one owns. I don't know what it is to see — but I know what it is to want to keep someone.
ione_letters4: When you hold all six embers, call me. I will no longer ask you to give them to me. I will help you let them go.
ione_letters_some: You carry {n} of my mother's letters — I feel the wax. She always wrote three at a time. Find the others.
ione_hint_dash: The old gravedigger still digs beneath the Cemetery, south of the Market. The dead say he has something that will help you cross the Bridge.
ione_hint_r2: Beyond the Bridge lies the Bastion of Vigils. Sir Caedmon never left the Watch — the first ember will be up there.
ione_hint_r3: Hilde worked in the Forges, beneath the Bastion. The cistern goes down there, if you can climb the walls.
ione_hint_r4: In the Pit where you woke there is a cracked wall. Behind it lie the nurse's Gardens. With Hilde's blow, you might break it.
ione_hint_r5: The Lower Belfry rises to the Tower of Bells, but it is too high for a single jump. Corvin lives up there, among the bells.
ione_hint_r6: Past the bells is the Cathedral, behind a veil that only parts for one who knows the right song. The bishop waits at the High Altar.
ione_hint_r7: The Palace gate, in the Square, recognises five embers. My father is inside, on the throne. Go when you are ready.
ione_hint_r7b: You read me the letters. When my father falls, I will come to you at the throne. Do not forget what my mother asked.
hrolf_meet1: Another one who walks straight! Welcome to the forge — or what's left of it. I'm Hrolf, apprentice to Master Hilde.
hrolf_meet2: The master went down to the Forges on the moonless night and never came back. I stayed to guard the anvil. Someone has to keep the fire lit, eh?
hrolf_meet3: Bring me Ash Steel and ash, and I'll temper that blade. As far as I know how — the rest, only the master knew.
hrolf_greet: Well? Does the blade need fire?
hrolf_greet_wait: You went down to the Forges? Did you… did you see the master?
hrolf_greet_after: The forge is hot. The master would be proud — or grumbling. With her it was the same thing.
hrolf_lore1: The master said the bishop ordered a cup no metal could withstand. She made it anyway. She was strange after that. Quiet.
hrolf_lore2: I moved to the Sanctuary. Lady Ione shouldn't be alone — and the market forge had no roof left.
hrolf_lore_after: Sometimes I strike with her hammer and hear her correcting me: "slower, boy". I was never a slow sort of boy.
hrolf_hammer1: That hammer… it's hers. Where did you find it? Is the master… is she all right?
hrolf_hammer2: You went down to the Forges. You know what happened. Tell me.
opt_truth: Tell the truth: she could not rest, and I set her free.
opt_lie: Lie: she is alive, somewhere in the deepest Forges.
hrolf_truth1: …So that's it. The ember wouldn't let her stop, just as nothing ever let her stop in life.
hrolf_truth2: Thank you for not lying to me. She hated lies almost as much as badly tempered steel.
hrolf_truth3: Take this. I made a new edge with her hammer, her way. Now I can temper the way she taught me — all the way.
hrolf_lie1: Alive? I knew it! She's as stubborn as an anvil!
hrolf_lie2: I'm going to fetch her. Don't look at me like that — I know the Forges better than anyone. Mind the forge for me, will you?
hrolf_chalice1: That chalice… it has the master's mark inside. A flaw shaped like a flame. She put it there on purpose — I know her stroke.
hrolf_chalice2: I can close it. But then the chalice will hold whatever you pour into it. Forever. Do you truly want that?
hrolf_body1: (Hrolf lies among the slag, his hammer still in hand. He came down looking for a master who was no longer here.)
hrolf_body2: (You take his hammer. It is the only thing you can still do for him.)
maren_meet1: Ah — no, don't strike me, I still breathe! Maren, pilgrim and merchant, at your service. I came into Vesperal three vespers ago and I can't get out.
maren_meet2: I'm looking for my brother, Teodoro. He was an acolyte of the bishop. No one has seen him since the moonless night.
maren_meet3: Take this medal. If you find him, show it to him — he'll know I sent you. And if you need things, I sell. Here, ash serves as coin.
maren_greet: Still in one piece? Good. Dead customers don't buy.
maren_greet_after: My brother is lighting candles without a licence. The bishop would have a fit. What have you got to spend?
maren_lore1: Someone saw an acolyte fleeing to the Gardens on the moonless night. The Gardens lie past the Pit where the dead wake… but there's a wall.
maren_lore2: Have you seen Teodoro? Tell me you've seen him. Tell me he's all right.
maren_lore_after: He told me what he did. He carried the chalice that night. I told him carrying isn't the same as filling.
maren_reunited1: Teodoro is in the Sanctuary! You sent him to me. I don't know how to repay you… yes, I do. Take this.
maren_reunited2: It's the rosary I prayed on for him. I don't need it for that anymore.
msg_maren_left: Maren's stall is empty. She left without saying goodbye.
teo_meet1: Don't touch me! No… you're not like the others. The others don't speak.
teo_meet2: I didn't do anything. I only held it. I only held the chalice, that's all.
teo_nomedal: Go away. I don't trust anyone who walks after death. I only trust my sister — and she isn't here.
teo_medal1: That medal… it's Maren's! My sister is alive? She's in Vesperal?
teo_medal2: I carried the chalice on the moonless night. The bishop promised no one would die. Then the light… the light shattered, and I ran.
teo_medal3: Tell me what to do. I don't know anymore.
opt_teo_sister: Go to your sister, in the Sanctuary.
opt_teo_cathedral: Go back to the Cathedral and face what you did.
teo_go_sister: Maren… yes. I'll go. Thank you. If the way is clear, I'll be there before vespers.
teo_go_cathedral: …You're right. I've run too long. I'll go to the Cathedral. If the bishop is still there, he will have to hear me.
teo_stay: I'll stay. No one looks for me here.
teo_key1: You're here! Maren told me everything. I… know something that might help you.
teo_key2: The bishop hid a key in the choir — the Ossuary key, beneath the Cemetery. I took it when I fled. Keep it.
teo_wait: Maren won't let me leave the Sanctuary. She says I've run enough for one lifetime.
teo_truth1: The bishop… fell? Then I can say it. I saw something in the chalice that night.
teo_truth2: Inside, a hairline crack shaped like a flame. It wasn't a defect: it was a signature. Master Hilde made the chalice to break.
teo_truth3: And the bishop… the bishop wasn't going to keep it on an altar. He was going to drink it. I heard him pray to be the last vessel. The eternal one.
teo_after: I lit a candle without a licence. Then another. No one came to arrest me. It's strange, being free.
teo_body1: (Teodoro lies before the reliquary, on his knees. He came to face what he did, and the Cathedral did not forgive him.)
teo_body2: (In his hand, an iron key and a note: "Maren — I'm sorry. I was brave once.")
teo_body3: (You keep the key. Maren will miss him before you can tell her.)
caedmon_pre1: Halt. The Watch has been sealed since the moonless night. No one passes without defeating me — and no one defeats me.
caedmon_pre2: Show me the guard you swore, dead one. If you cannot parry, you know nothing.
caedmon_post1: …Well parried. She parried like that too — laughing, when I taught her.
caedmon_post2: Take the ember. Tell the girl the captain kept watch to the end. And let me, at last, sit down.
hilde_pre1: Who sent you? The bishop? Tell him the cup is made, and that I did exactly what was asked. Exactly.
hilde_pre2: Or have you come for the ember? Then come. But I warn you: I forge better than I talk.
hilde_mid: Still standing? Good metal is like that. Let's see if you can take the whole fire!
hilde_post1: Ah… the fire's gone out. What a relief, child. What a relief.
hilde_post2: Tell my boy, Hrolf… no. Tell him the truth. He deserves the truth more than I deserved forgiveness.
elowen_pre1: Shhh. The little one is sleeping. Don't wake the little one.
elowen_pre2: Who are you? I don't know you. I don't know you! Go away before she wakes!
elowen_mid: Cry, cry, the water rises… sleep, sleep, nurse won't let go…
elowen_post1: Seraphine? You've grown so tall… and so cold. Let me sing you just one more.
elowen_post2: Sleep, little flame… the night is long… and nurse… is tired too…
corvin_pre1: An audience! How long it's been! Sit — no, stand, this is no music for sitting.
corvin_pre2: Every note is a blow and every blow is a note. Lose the beat and you lose your head. One, two, three…
corvin_mid2: The finale, the finale! I played it once for the queen. She wept. You will dance!
corvin_post1: Ah… the music's over. Do you know which song was forbidden? The Song of Morning. It tells of a light that is born and dies every day.
corvin_post2: She asked me to play it again. I promised her one day I'd play it to the true sun. Take the ember. Perhaps you'll keep the promise.
ozias_pre1: So you are the one gathering what I failed to keep. Kneel, child. This is a holy place.
ozias_pre2: I wanted to save her. That no queen would ever burn again. That the Church would bear the burden — that I would bear it.
ozias_pre3: The smith betrayed me. You will not. Give me the embers and I will be the last vessel. The eternal one. No one else will suffer.
ozias_mid1: Don't you understand? Without a vessel, Vesperal does not sleep!
ozias_mid2: See the light, child! See it and kneel!
ozias_post1: I taught her to read… and she read things I never taught her. Old books. She spoke of mornings.
ozias_post2: The chalice is yours now. May God give you more sense than He gave me.
vael_post: The light… unlicensed… still shines. How strange.
gemeos_post: Together… to the end. As we swore. Pass, then. The king awaits you.
aldric_pre1: You came. I knew someone would. Warm yourself by the fire, dead one. It is the last fire in the kingdom.
aldric_pre2: She asked me not to save her. I did not listen. I saved her until she broke into six.
aldric_pre3: This ember is all I have left of her. I will not give it to you. You will have to tear it from me, as I tore it from her.
aldric_mid1: Do you feel it? It is her! She burns in me as she burned in herself! And all those she loved burn with me!
aldric_mid2: You will not take her! YOU WILL NOT TAKE HER!
aldric_post1: …It is so cold, suddenly. Is this what she felt when I held her hand?
aldric_post2: Tell Ione… that her father always heard her. Even when he pretended not to.
aldric_post3: Take it. The ember. Take it wherever it wants to go.
seraphine_pre1: Ah. It is you. I waited so long for you to wake.
seraphine_pre2: I am what remained of me inside the flame. Before you let it go, let me see if you are able to let go. Return the light I give you.
seraphine_mid1: Yes. You don't hold it — you return it. That is how one loves what is not ours.
seraphine_mid2: A little more. The sky already remembers its colour.
seraphine_post: Thank you. Now — look up. Both of you. Look up.
carpideira_post: No one… needs me… to weep anymore.
chalice_found: (Among the bishop's ashes lies the chalice of Ozias. A thin flaw runs inside it, shaped like a flame. What do you do with it?)
final_ione1: I followed the warmth. You are here — and my father is not. I feel the six embers with you.
final_ione2: We have reached the end. Tell me what we do with them.
final_ask: The six embers burn in your hands. What do you do?
final_opt1: Give the embers to Ione, to rekindle the Last Flame.
final_opt2: Pour the embers into the Mended Chalice and drink.
final_opt3: Do what the queen asked: release the Lume.
final_letters1: You remember the letters. I do not ask for them. Let us let them go.
end1_l1: Ione held out her hands, and you gave her the six embers.
end1_l2: The Last Flame was rekindled in the Sanctuary. Across the city, the dead lay down where they stood and closed their eyes.
end1_l3: You too felt sleep arrive, heavy and good, as it comes to those who have worked hard.
end1_l4: Ione did not weep. She said that, for the first time, she could see something: a light, within, filling her chest.
end1_l5: Vesperal remained in twilight. Ione burned slowly, like her mother, and was the wisest queen the kingdom ever had.
end2_l1: You poured the six embers into the chalice Hrolf had mended. The light filled it without breaking it.
end2_l2: You drank. The dead do not burn — they keep. The Lume found in you a vessel that never ends.
end2_l3: The Last Flame lit within you. The dead of Vesperal slept. No queen was ever chosen again.
end2_l4: Ione left through the Eastern Gates to see the world. She promised to visit. She never said when.
end2_l5: You remained on the throne of ash, burning without being consumed, while the twilight of Vesperal became eternal.
end2_l6: The bishop was right about one thing: someone had to bear the burden.
end3_l1: You opened your hands, and Ione opened hers.
end3_l2: The six embers rose together, slowly, like those who know the way home.
end3_l3: They passed through the Palace roof, the clouds of ash, the twilight of a thousand years.
end3_l4: And for the first time since the first kings, the sky of Vesperal changed colour.
end3_l5: Ione turned her face to the east. She could not see. But she felt the warmth on her cheeks, and laughed the way her mother laughed.
end3_l6: The dead rested. You did too — and the last thing you saw was the light being born, belonging to no one.
end3_l7: For the first time, morning came.
chr_awake: I woke in a pit of ash, with no name and no memory. Something small and warm burns in my chest. The other dead walk, but they do not think. I think.
chr_ione: In the Sanctuary, Ione — blind daughter of Queen Seraphine — asked me to gather the six embers of the Lume, which fled to those the queen loved. Only then, she says, will the Last Flame burn again and the dead sleep once more.
chr_ember1: Sir Caedmon, the queen's shield, kept the first ember at the Watch. His guard was never for the Palace: it was for her.
chr_ember2: Master Hilde forged the bishop's chalice and kept the second ember in the Forges. Between blows she said no metal can hold the Lume — as if she had known before she began.
chr_hrolf: I told Hrolf what became of his master. What I said decided the path he took.
chr_ember3: Nurse Elowen cradled the third ember like a baby. She raised the queen and the princess, and still called them by their girlhood names.
chr_teodoro: Teodoro, the bishop's acolyte, carried the chalice on the moonless night. I told him where to go. Whatever the path, there is no going back.
chr_ember4: Corvin the minstrel kept the fourth ember atop the Tower and fought to the rhythm of his own music. He told me of a forbidden song: the Song of Morning.
chr_ember5: Bishop Ozias wanted no queen to burn again — so long as he was the one to keep the light. The fifth ember was his.
chr_chalice: I decided the fate of the chalice of Ozias. Whole, it may still hold the Lume. Broken, it is only a memory.
chr_letters: I found the queen's three letters. Seraphine knew everything: the chalice, the flaw, the embers. And me — or someone like me.
chr_ember6: King Aldric waited on the throne of ash with the last ember. He loved her too much to let her go, and so he lost her twice.
chr_end1: I gave the embers to Ione. The Last Flame burned again, and with it the old cycle.
chr_end2: I drank the Lume from the mended chalice. I keep it now, forever — and Vesperal will never see morning.
chr_end3: With Ione, I let the Lume return to the sky. Vesperal saw its first morning in a thousand years.
letter_1_text:
Ione, my little one,

when you read this — or when someone reads it to you, for you never needed eyes to know where I was — I will be gone.

The Lume will flee from me when the chalice breaks, and it will seek those I love. So in the last moment I will do the hardest thing of my life: I will not think of you. Not once. So that the flame will not find you.

Forgive me that silence. It was the greatest love I knew how to give.

— Your mother
letter_2_text:
Aldric,

I know what the bishop promised you and I know why you agreed. I don't blame you. Watching someone burn slowly is worse than burning.

But do not save me. Love me until the end; that is all I ask. And when I am gone, do not keep the flame in anyone. Not even in yourself.

If you keep it, Vesperal will never see what I see in dreams: the sky changing colour.

— Yours, Seraphine
letter_3_text:
To whoever wakes,

I do not know your name. Perhaps you no longer know it yourself. If you are reading this, Hilde did what I asked and the chalice broke.

The Lume is not a flame: it is the morning the first kings stole from the sky and locked inside bodies like mine. That is why it burns, why it chooses, why it never accepts an owner — it is searching for its way home.

Gather the six embers. Do not give them to anyone to keep — not even my daughter, however much she asks.

Read these letters to Ione. She cannot see the light, so she does not crave it. Only she can let it go.

And when the sky changes colour, rest. You have earned it.

— S.
ins_i01: Here lies one who left no name. May the Flame guide them to rest, if it still burns.
ins_i02: By order of the Palace: no candle is to be lit after the vesper bell. The light belongs to the Queen.
ins_i03: The Lume chooses. It is not asked for, it is not refused. While the vessel burns, the Last Flame burns, and the dead sleep.
ins_i04:
Seraphine, Vessel of the Lume, Queen of Vesperal. Chosen at seven. Crowned at nineteen.
"I burn so that you may sleep."
ins_i05: She prayed here alone, without a bishop. She said the flame spoke to her of something the ancients called morning.
ins_i06: I dug for kings and for beggars. Since the moonless night, no one stays in the earth. I dig all the same; it is what I know how to do.
ins_i07: The bones of the first kings wear no crowns. Each holds a small bronze cup between its hands.
ins_i08: I swear to guard the Vessel from the first breath to the last. Not the crown, not the Palace: her.
ins_i09: Third night of rain. The captain does not sleep. He stands on the Watch, facing the Palace, as if there were still someone to guard.
ins_i10:
Spears: 40. Shields: 38. Candles: 0 (requisitioned by the Palace).
Note: since no one sleeps, the men see better in the dark.
ins_i11: They say that before the walls there was a sky that changed colour. The old ones say many things.
ins_i12: Meltwater from the Forges. Do not drink after curfew — it comes out hot.
ins_i13:
Here we cast whatever the Palace commands. We do not ask what for.
— Master Hilde
(Below, in another hand: "I ask.")
ins_i14: Forge automaton, model III. Feed with embers at every bell. Never turn your back on the furnace — nor does he.
ins_i15: The bishop wants a chalice that can hold the Lume. No metal can hold the Lume. I told him so. He smiled and paid double.
ins_i16: To Seraphine, who taught me to read, and whom I taught to hold a hammer. One of us got the better part.
ins_i17:
For a piece to break when full: a flaw shaped like a flame, on the inside, where no bishop looks.
She asked it of me. May the gods forgive me — or may she, which is the same.
ins_i18:
Winter roses. Planted by Princess Seraphine at eight, with Nurse Elowen.
"For when there is morning," the girl wrote.
ins_i19: The pond rises a hand's breadth for every tear the nurse sheds. Since the moonless night, the bench where she sat can no longer be seen.
ins_i20: Moths seek the light and die in it. Some call it love. The nurse said it is only hunger.
ins_i21:
Sleep, sleep, little flame,
the night is long, your mother calls your name;
when morning comes back to the sky,
the fire is yours, the sleep is I.
ins_i22: Silence. The nurse rocks what she has left. Whoever wakes the cradle wakes her.
ins_i23: The bells mark the vespers. There is no other hour in Vesperal. Whoever asks for another hour will be heard by the bishop.
ins_i24: From here you can see the horizon. It is red at one point — always the same point. Corvin says that is where the sun is imprisoned.
ins_i25:
"Song of Morning", by an ancient author. Forbidden by the Palace.
Corvin played it once for the Queen. She wept and asked for it again.
ins_i26: Cast from the bronze of the first kings' cups. When it rings, the whole city remembers that it has an owner.
ins_i27: Enter on your knees. The light you see here was lent by the Vessel. Repay it with obedience.
ins_i28: In the beginning, the light was born and died every day, and no one owned it. The first kings found this intolerable.
ins_i29: …and they kept the morning in a cup, and the cup in a body, and the body on a throne. And they called it Lume, so that no one would remember the old name.
ins_i30: Acolytes present on the moonless night: Teodoro (chalice bearer). The rest fled. Teodoro too, afterwards.
ins_i31:
Ozias, bishop of Vesperal: "Let no queen burn again. Let the Church bear the burden."
No one asked him whether the burden was his to bear.
ins_i32:
Through here the chosen enter. Through here they do not leave.
(Ancient royal motto)
ins_i33: Tonight she laughed at something I said, and for an instant she did not glow. I would give the kingdom for one more instant like that. Perhaps I will.
ins_i34: Seraphine, painted on the day of her coronation. The painter complained that he could not look at her for more than a minute at a time.
ins_i35: The throne of Vesperal was made for whoever keeps the light. No one made it for whoever sets it free.
item_ab_dash_desc: The gravedigger kept it without knowing. Press Dodge in the air to launch yourself forward, across chasms no jump can reach.
item_ab_spell_desc: A spark of the Lume that Ione taught you to release. Costs a third of your Lume; Lume refills when you strike and parry.
item_ab_wall_desc: Caedmon's last gift: to cling to stone as he clung to his oath. Doubles climbing stamina, climbs faster, lets you spring up the wall and leap from wall to wall.
item_ab_forge_desc: Hilde taught you, without words, to charge a blow. Hold the heavy attack until it glows: it breaks cracked stone.
item_ab_double_desc: Wing dust that still remembers flight. Jump a second time in the air.
item_ab_veil_desc: Corvin sang the veil until it came undone. You pass through spectral barriers.
item_ember_1_desc: It burns with a bluish light, steady as a shield. Ione will know what to do with it.
item_ember_2_desc: Hot as a lit forge. Hold it to your ear and it sounds like a hammer.
item_ember_3_desc: Warm, almost asleep. It weighs like a baby in your arms.
item_ember_4_desc: It throbs to a rhythm that is not yours.
item_ember_5_desc: Golden outside and cold within, like a promise badly made.
item_ember_6_desc: The heaviest of the six. It burns like grief.
item_letter_1_desc: A letter from the queen, sealed with red wax. You can reread it in the inventory or the Journal.
item_letter_2_desc: A letter from the queen to Aldric, never delivered. You can reread it in the inventory or the Journal.
item_letter_3_desc: A letter from the queen hidden behind a false wall. Addressed to someone she never knew.
item_chalice_desc: The chalice that was meant to hold the Lume. A thin crack shaped like a flame runs inside it. A smith might know how to mend it.
item_chalice_mended_desc: Hrolf closed the flaw with his master's technique. Now it can hold the Lume — and whoever drinks from it will never stop keeping it.
item_ossuary_key_desc: Opens the iron door at the bottom of the Cemetery. The bishop hid it; Teodoro knew where.
item_bastion_key_desc: A heavy iron key that no lock answers to.
item_palace_seal_desc: The seal of the Twin Guards. Whoever carries it fought for the king — or against him.
item_hilde_hammer_desc: The master smith's hammer, still warm. Hrolf will want to see it.
item_teodoro_medal_desc: An acolyte's medal that Maren gave you. Teodoro will recognise it.
item_elowen_lullaby_desc: A folded paper that lay in Elowen's cradle. The handwriting is a girl's: "for when there is morning".
item_ash_steel_desc: Steel tempered in the ash of the dead. Hrolf uses it to improve your blade.
item_candle_fragment_desc: Wax from an old votive candle. It joins your candles: one more at every rest.
item_ash_heart_desc: A heart that stopped beating but not warming. Increases your maximum health.
item_relic_slot_desc: A silver setting: you can equip one more relic.
item_oil_desc: Coat the blade: for one minute, your strikes deal more damage.
item_incense_desc: The smoke hardens the skin: for one minute, you take less damage.
item_salt_desc: A pinch of blessed salt. Restores some health instantly, without pausing.
item_feather_desc: A feather that knows the way home. Takes you to the last Altar where you rested.
item_r_rosary_desc: The beads Maren prayed on for her brother. Healing with a candle is faster.
item_r_amber_desc: Amber that held light for centuries. Candles heal more.
item_r_raven_eye_desc: A glass eye that sees through what is false. Reveals false walls with a faint glow.
item_r_heron_desc: Light as a heron. You move faster.
item_r_captain_desc: Sir Caedmon's signet. The parry window is wider.
item_r_ember_desc: A coal from Vael's censer. The Spark deals more damage.
item_r_hrolf_hammer_desc: The apprentice's hammer, found beside him. Heavy attacks deal more damage.
item_r_chalice_shard_desc: A piece of the chalice you shattered. When you are close to falling, you deal more damage.
item_r_ione_ribbon_desc: The ribbon that tied Ione's hair. You gather more ash.
item_r_hairshirt_desc: A penitent's belt of thorns. Taking damage grants you Lume.
item_r_anchor_desc: An anchor weight tied to your belt. You are not knocked back when hurt.
item_r_lantern_desc: A lantern that never goes out. More light around you, and Lume returns faster.
item_r_hilde_blade_desc: Hrolf's last work with his master's hammer: a new edge for your blade. Your strikes deal more damage.
enj_husk: The city's dead. They wander aimlessly, but they still remember how to hate whatever moves.
enj_crawler: Those who fell face down and stayed that way. They bite ankles.
enj_wisp: A spark that broke away from someone and never found its way back. Its fireballs can be returned with a parry.
enj_sexton: Keepers of the snuffed candles. The lantern is the only light they have left, and they defend it. When they set it down with a red glow, back away.
enj_sentinel: Soldiers of the Bastion. The shield stops blows from the front; a heavy strike, the Spark or their back will do. The thrust gleams — parry it.
enj_crossbow: The bolts gleam before they fly. A parry at the right moment sends them back.
enj_hound: The guard dogs kept on guarding. No one told them to stop.
enj_thrall: Chained to the anvils in life, and in death. The red hammer blow cannot be parried — dodge it.
enj_slag: Molten metal that learned to crawl. It splits when it dies.
enj_smelter: They hurl molten metal in an arc. Do not linger where it lands.
enj_thornmaid: Gardeners who let themselves take root while waiting for the nurse. The vine whip warns with a gleam.
enj_drowned: They sleep beneath the shallow water and wake to the warmth of passers-by.
enj_moth: They seek the light. You are light.
enj_gargoyle: Statues that remember having wings. Motionless until you pass beneath.
enj_acolyte: They ring the vespers forever. The bell's waves hurt; jump over them.
enj_raven: They eat what the ash leaves behind.
enj_penitent: They punished themselves in life to deserve the light. They keep punishing whoever brings it. The third blow gleams.
enj_vitrail: The saints of the stained glass came down from the windows. A heavy strike shatters them best.
enj_choir: Stone heads from the choir, still singing. Their song spreads in a circle.
enj_royalguard: The king's personal guard. They change their strike midway — read the glow.
enj_courtier: Ghosts of the court. They appear behind you, as in life. They can only be hurt while visible.
enj_torch: Servants who have burned since the moonless night. When they flare red, back away.
enj_husk_big: A Husk that never stopped growing beneath the ash. Slow to raise its arm — and when it brings it down, the street shakes.
enj_hound_big: The captain's dog, as big as a horse. The collar still bears its name, but no one gets close enough to read it.
enj_thrall_big: They gave it more chains than any other, and it carried them all. The red hammer blow splits the floor — dodge far away.
enj_drowned_big: The first to lie down in the pond, when the garden still had flowers. Its claws grew along with the roots.
enj_gargoyle_big: It guarded the great bell. When it dives, the wind of its wings arrives first.
enj_penitent_big: It carried the heaviest yoke in the procession until the yoke grew into its shoulders. Every blow weighs like a bell; the third one gleams.
enj_royalguard_big: It won every tourney in the realm and was set to guard the throne room door. The halberd reaches farther than you think.
bossj_coveiro: The city's gravedigger kept digging after he died. Without knowing, he kept the Ash Step.
bossj_matilheira: The oldest bitch in the Bastion kennels. She called her pups whenever she was wounded.
bossj_caedmon: Sir Caedmon, the Queen's Shield. His shield never yielded to a blow — only to a perfect parry.
bossj_automato: Forge automaton, model III. The furnace on its back was both its weakness and its heart.
bossj_hilde: Master Hilde, smith, childhood friend of the queen. She forged the chalice — and the flaw within it.
bossj_mariposa: The mother of all the moths in the Gardens. She died seeking the light, like her daughters. She left you her wings.
bossj_elowen: Nurse Elowen raised the queen and the princess. She cradled the ember as she cradled them both.
bossj_sineiro: The Bellringer rang the great vesper bell — and fought with it still bound to its chain.
bossj_corvin: Corvin, court minstrel. He played the Song of Morning for the queen and fought to the beat of his last music.
bossj_vael: Inquisitor Vael, the bishop's right hand. She hunted those who lit candles without licence.
bossj_ozias: Ozias, bishop of Vesperal, the queen's confessor. He wanted to end the sacrifice — by becoming the eternal one himself.
bossj_gemeos: The Twin Guards, Blade and Maul. They swore never to fight apart.
bossj_aldric: Aldric, king of Vesperal. He accepted the bishop's plan because he could not bear to watch her burn.
bossj_seraphine: The Echo of Seraphine: what remained of the queen inside the Lume. She did not ask you to win; she asked you to let go.
bossj_carpideira: She wept for the city's dead as a trade, so much per funeral. When the whole city died there was no one left to pay her — and she wept for them all, for nothing, until her voice broke. She still drifts from room to room, looking for someone to mourn.
bossj_custodio: The monstrance where the light was shown to the people on feast days. When the light went out, only the gold remained — and the gold opened an eye. It knows no fear, no weariness, no pain: only radiance.
item_w_desperto_desc:
An old iron sword with an engraved fuller and drooping quillons, found in your own grave. No one carved a name on it.

Balanced: neither fast nor slow, good for almost anything. Three strikes in a row; the heavy strike lunges forward.
item_w_navalhas_desc:
A pair of curved razors with horn grips and brass ferrules, taken from the Old Pack-Mother's collars.

They cut four times while another weapon cuts once. Strong against agile creatures; nearly useless against armour and stone.
item_w_malho_desc:
A maul torn from the chest of the Bellows Automaton. Its head still holds a vein of ember.

Slow and heavy. Breaks shields and guards and crushes armour. When charged, it sends shockwaves along the ground.
item_w_alabarda_desc:
A halberd of the queen's old guard, with a red tassel and the sun engraved in the iron. Maren says she traded bread for it.

Keeps danger at a distance and reaches what flies. The heavy strike sweeps both in front and behind.
item_w_espirito_desc:
A blade of stained glass bound with lead, forgotten among the bones of the Ossuary. It kindles with the light of whoever holds it.

Wounds spectres and things made of light like no other; it glances off armour. The third strike and the charged strike release a spirit wave.
item_w_montante_desc:
King Aldric's greatsword: black steel with a vein of ember and a golden guard set with suns. It weighs like a crown.

The strongest weapon in the kingdom. Wide, slow strikes that break armour and leave embers in the air.
item_look_capuz_desc: The hood, the gold-mended porcelain mask and the wine-red tabard you woke up in, in the grave.
item_helm_sino_desc:
A bronze helm cast from a cracked bell, with a cross-shaped slit and a linen ribbon. Whoever wears it hears vespers even in silence.

Outfit: changes the Awakened's appearance. Swap it in the inventory, under Weapons.
msg_final_ready: The King's Greatsword is yours. Speak to Ione by the throne when you are ready — until then, the kingdom waits.
final_wait: I am in no hurry. There are still people out there who need you. When you are ready, come back — I will be here, by the throne.
final_ready_ask: I hear your footsteps. Are you ready to decide what we do with the Lume?
tip_coveiro_back: With his spade stuck in the ground, the Gravedigger cannot see behind him — strike at the lantern on his back!
tip_aldric_wall: The king cannot stop mid-charge: let him crash into the wall or the throne dais and punish him while he is down!
ins_i36: Deep grooves in the stone at shoulder height, and flakes of gold on the floor. When the king charges he cannot stop: put a wall before him and he ends up on his back.
tip_matilheira_belly: When she howls, the Pack-Mother rears up and shows her belly — strike there! A heavy blow cuts the howl short.
ins_i37: The handlers knew: the old one only rears up to call the pack, and whoever rears up shows their belly. One good blow there and no one answers her.
ins_i38: "No strength shall make me yield." Beneath it, another hand scratched: only the right moment. Turn his blow aside the instant his blade gleams, three times, and the queen's shield opens.
hint_move_touch: Move: left joystick · Jump: ⇧ · Attack: sword · Dodge: ⇒
hint_attack_touch: Attack: sword button (joystick up or down for directional strikes) · Heavy strike: hammer
hint_heal_touch: Heal: candle button · Parry: shield at the moment of impact; hold to guard
hint_move_pad: Move: left stick · Jump: A · Attack: X · Dodge: B
hint_attack_pad: Attack: X (with ↑ or ↓ for directional strikes) · Heavy strike: Y
hint_heal_pad: Heal: LB · Parry: RB at the moment of impact; hold to guard
ins_i39: I counted the bells: every time the floor spits fire, the colossus burns inside and forgets to turn around. The grate on its back glows white. There, and only there.
tip_hilde_heat: The hammer has turned white-hot and burned her hands — Hilde lets go. Strike now!
ins_i40_t: Workshop Rule, Carved on the Lintel
ins_i40: Three blows and the iron begs for water. Whoever holds a white-hot hammer lets it go, even the master. Count the blows; wait for the white.
tip_mariposa_rest: After shedding her dust, the Moth Mother lands exhausted, wings folded. Strike her on the ground!
tip_carpideira_scream: The scream can't be parried or jumped: dodge through the waves.
tip_carpideira_tired: After the double scream she falls to her knees, exhausted. Now!
tip_custodio_rays: The rays turn — outrun them or dodge through.
tip_custodio_blades: Parry the golden blades: they fly back and wound him.
tip_custodio_parry: He is all light: weapons pass through him. Only parries hurt him — parry his light strikes at the gleam.
tip_custodio_eclipse: Eclipse! In the dark, only the gleam of his blade warns you — parry it.
msg_wail_far: Somewhere far off, someone is weeping.
ins_i41_t: A Gardener's Note, Pinned to a Thorn
ins_i41: Don't climb to meet her. She shakes the dust from her wings and the dust weighs on her; then she comes down, folds her wings like a roof and sleeps a little. It is in that short sleep that one prunes.
tip_elowen_song: Elowen closes her eyes and rocks the bundle, singing — interrupt the song!
tip_elowen_broken: The song breaks. Elowen bends over the empty bundle.
ins_i42_t: A Child's Scrawl on the Cradle Wall
ins_i42: Nanny sings with her eyes closed and sees nothing. If we wake her before the end, she cries and forgets about us. (Below, in another hand: don't let her finish the song.)
tip_sineiro_parry: You parried the bell — its toll burst in his ears. The Bellringer is dazed!
tip_sineiro_dazed: The bell rang against his head again!
ins_i43: Brother bell-ringer no longer hears, but he still feels. When the bell swings back and strikes his hood, he staggers like a drunk for a good while. Don't flee the swing: send it back.
set_video_note: If the game isn't smooth, choose Medium or Low quality and a 60 limit. Automatic lowers the internal resolution on its own when the PC can't keep up.
hint_climb: Against a wall in mid-air: ↑ climbs, ↓ slides. Stamina refills on the ground.
hint_climb_touch: Against a wall in mid-air: push the stick up to climb, down to slide.
hint_climb_pad: Against a wall in mid-air: stick ↑ climbs, ↓ slides. Stamina refills on the ground.
tip_corvin_climb: The song turns aside anything from below. Climb to Corvin's balcony, parry his notes back at him — or wait for him to come down.
tip_corvin_groggy: Corvin is dazed from the fall — punish him now!
tip_repel: Bosses answer non-stop hammering: at the red glow, back off or dodge through the shockwave.
tip_corvin_beat: On the beat of the music, a blow cuts deeper.
ins_i44_t: Torn Score, Pinned to the Column
ins_i44: The minstrel comes down for no one. He plays from the bell balconies and his music pushes away rising steel. Whoever would silence him must climb: the walls, the column, the corbels where breath returns. And strike on the beat — he taught that himself.
tip_caedmon_volley: "Shields up!" — the dead archers loose their arrows. Shelter under his pavise!
tip_matilheira_wall: The Old Pack-Mother is out of breath after her rampage: strike now! (Climb the wall or the platforms to escape the charge.)
tip_vael_stuck: The flail's ball is stuck in the floor! Strike while Vael wrenches it free.
tip_gemeos_friendly: The Maul can't tell brothers apart: put the Blade between you and the blow.
tip_ozias_orb: The chalice orb can be sent back: parry it as it arrives.
tip_aldric_judgement: The King's Judgement kills in one blow: jump over the crimson wave or dodge through it!
tip_seraphine_wings: A wall of light feathers is coming: slip into its gap as it passes, or dodge through it.
tip_seraphine_time: Time has stopped: her light hangs in the air. Leave the ring of lances through its gap (or dodge through it) before time returns!
tip_seraphine_rewind: Time unravels: the light that already passed comes back — watch your back.
item_ab_dashstrike_desc: The hounds' stride. Attack in the middle of a dodge to cut through everything in your path without losing your invulnerability.
tut_dashstrike: Cutting Rush: attack in the middle of a dodge to cut through everything in your path.
item_ab_counter_desc: What Nurse Elowen kept for other people's children. After a parry, your riposte releases a crescent of light that passes through up to three enemies.
tut_counter: Counter-Light: attack after a parry — the riposte releases a crescent of light.
item_ab_instinct_desc: The bell-ringer could hear the time between two tolls. A last-instant dodge slows the world for a moment (you keep your speed).
tut_instinct: Instinct: dodge at the last instant and the world slows down for a moment.
res_parry_only: Weapons pass through him: only parries hurt him.
tip_pattern: Dodge pattern: read the warnings on the floor and the gaps — it cannot be parried, only dodged.
tip_aldric_drain: Royal Bloodletting: if the chain catches you, the king drains your life — dodge or get away to break it!
tip_aldric_heal: The king is recovering his life — four hits (or two heavy ones) interrupt him and knock him down!
trials_welcome: The Tower of Trials: ring the great bell to choose a trial. Dying here costs no ash.
trials_text: The tower's bells fell across the kingdom. Those that still ring call the trials: endure the guardians' light, or face their echo, harder than they ever were.
trials_dodge_text: The Voice of the tower casts the guardians' attacks one after another. Endure to the end. There is nothing to strike: only to dodge.
trials_echo_text: The guardians you defeated, once more, in their own halls: more life, more fury. The first victory over each echo is rewarded.
trials_echo_none: You have not defeated any guardian yet.
msg_bells_returned: The bell rings in the tower once more. Bells returned: {n}/{m}.
item_lost_bell_desc: One of the bells of the Tower of Trials, fallen in a room no one knows. Return it to the tower's great bell.
item_r_tower_bell_desc: Silver that still hums. Instinct lasts longer and every perfect dodge gives you back a little Lume.
item_r_echo_crown_desc: Made from the ash the echoes leave behind. Your strikes hurt bosses more.
confirm_ngp: Start New Game+ on this save? The story starts over; you keep your weapons, relics, abilities, health and ash. Enemies and bosses become much stronger.
